idea: Order groceries online for home delivery
lesson: Webvan spent over $1B on its own automated warehouses and trucks before demand existed and died in 2001, while Instacart a decade later sent gig shoppers into existing supermarkets and needed far less capital.

idea: Sell pet food and supplies online with home delivery
lesson: Pets.com shipped heavy, low-margin goods below cost in 2000, while Chewy launched in 2011 with cheaper logistics, repeat Autoship subscriptions and service-led loyalty, and sold to PetSmart for $3.35B.

idea: Book vetted cleaners and handymen through an app
lesson: Homejoy lost customers and cleaners off-platform after first bookings and was hit by US worker-classification lawsuits, while Handy survived to a 2018 sale and India's Urban Company built a trained, standardized workforce in a market without those legal pressures.

idea: Deliver convenience goods to your door in under an hour
lesson: Kozmo and Urbanfetch delivered small orders free and burned out in 2001, while Gopuff owned its inventory for retail margins, charged delivery fees and grew slowly from college towns before raising at $15B.

idea: Online social network of real friends
lesson: theglobe.com was too early, Friendster's site slowed to a crawl as it grew, and Myspace filled with spam after selling to News Corp, while Facebook expanded campus by campus on reliable infrastructure.

idea: Hail a ride from a nearby driver via smartphone
lesson: Sidecar pioneered peer-to-peer rides but was outspent by Uber, and Uber in turn sold its China and Southeast Asia businesses to local champions Didi and Grab and bought Careem, showing local capital and density usually beat a global entrant.

idea: Daily group-buying discounts at local merchants
lesson: Groupon and LivingSocial faded as merchants tired of deep discounts, while China's Meituan survived a brutal group-buying price war by turning its merchant network into food delivery.

idea: Shared dockless e-scooters rented by app
lesson: Bird kept expanding with costly, short-lived scooters and went bankrupt in 2023, while Lime took an Uber-led rescue round in 2020, cut costs and kept operating, and European operators competed for limited city permits.

idea: New electric-vehicle maker challenging incumbents
lesson: Tesla and Rivian spent years engineering with patient capital and anchor backers (a DOE loan, Amazon's van order) before scaling, while the 2020 SPAC-era EV startups went public before they had working products and were bankrupt by 2023-2025.

idea: Aggregate all your bank accounts into one budgeting app
lesson: Mint synced accounts automatically and sold to Intuit for $170M in 2009, while privacy-focused Wesabe required more manual work and shut down in 2010.

idea: Stream video games from cloud servers instead of local consoles
lesson: OnLive sold consumer subscriptions on costly per-user server hardware and collapsed in 2012, while Gaikai sold demo streaming to publishers and was bought by Sony for $380M the same year.

idea: AI that writes and completes code for programmers
lesson: Kite launched before large language models were good enough and shut in 2022, while Cursor and Windsurf arrived with GPT-4-class models; Windsurf, dependent on outside model providers, was split between Google and Cognition in 2025.

idea: Independent AI model lab or AI-native product company
lesson: Labs without distribution or a clear enterprise niche (Inflection, Adept, Character.AI, Covariant) let Big Tech hire their founders through licensing deals in 2024, while OpenAI's consumer breakout and Cohere's enterprise focus let them keep raising independently.

idea: Mobile app for sharing photos with friends
lesson: Color raised $41M before launch for a confusing proximity-based app and ended in an acquihire, while Instagram shipped one simple feature and sold to Facebook for $1B 18 months after launch.

idea: On-demand digital music streaming
lesson: Napster and Grooveshark ignored licensing and were shut down by courts, Rdio was licensed but outmarketed, while Pandora and Spotify licensed music from the start and survived to IPOs.

idea: Wrist-worn fitness tracker or smartwatch
lesson: Fitbit won with reliable hardware and retail distribution and IPO'd in 2015, while Jawbone's faulty bands and lawsuits ended in liquidation and Pebble sold its assets to Fitbit for $23M.

idea: Constellations of low-orbit satellites for global connectivity
lesson: Iridium and Teledesic failed in the late 1990s when launch and handset costs were too high, while SpaceX cut launch costs with reusable rockets and made Starlink work two decades later.

idea: Rent space short-term to users (desks, apartments) at scale
lesson: WeWork and Sonder signed long fixed leases and rented space short-term, which collapsed when demand fell, while Airbnb ran an asset-light marketplace of hosts' homes and owned no leases.

idea: Hold and grow retail customers' crypto deposits
lesson: Platforms that lent out, traded or misused customer deposits (QuadrigaCX, Celsius, BlockFi, Voyager, FTX) collapsed, while Coinbase, which held assets in custody under US regulation, survived every crash.

idea: Buy and sell used cars online with delivery
lesson: Beepi matched private sellers with buyers and ran out of money in 2017, while Carvana owned and reconditioned its inventory with financing from its dealer parent and went public the same year.

idea: Deliver freshly cooked meals on demand
lesson: Sprig and Munchery cooked every meal in their own kitchens and died of high costs, while DoorDash and Deliveroo only delivered restaurants' food and India's Rebel Foods ran many brands out of shared cloud kitchens.

idea: Subscription boxes of recipes and pre-portioned ingredients
lesson: Blue Apron stayed largely US-only with high churn and sold for $103M in 2023, while Germany's HelloFresh expanded across many countries and became the global category leader.

idea: Self-driving vehicle technology
lesson: Argo depended on two automaker backers who pulled out in 2022 and Cruise was shut by GM after a 2023 crash, while Aurora narrowed to highway trucking and launched driverless commercial runs in Texas in 2025.

idea: All-in-one HR, payroll and benefits software for small businesses
lesson: Zenefits gave software away and relied on insurance-broker commissions, which led to a licensing scandal, while the same founder's Rippling charged for software built on one employee database and became worth several times more.

idea: Mobile-only bank account with low or no fees
lesson: Chime grew in the US through partner banks and card interchange fees and Nubank grew in Brazil against high-fee incumbents, while N26 retreated from the US and UK to focus on Europe.
